title: Sabi exam format
description:
One exam's rules, as data rather than code (master prompt v2 §3.2). FROZEN CONTRACT between the content pipeline and exam mode.

Exam mode reads this and nothing else: question counts, durations, option labels, keyboard bindings, navigation and scoring all come from here, so adding NECO or a university's Post-UTME is a config file rather than a branch in the simulator. The conformance test for each exam is generated from its own config, which is only meaningful if the simulator has no hard-coded knowledge to disagree with it.

`source_url` and `verified_on` are REQUIRED. Nigerian exam formats change between seasons -- WAEC's CBT transition moved twice while this was being written -- so a config nobody can trace to an official page is a config nobody can re-check. A test fails any config without them.

institution.description: Required for POSTUTME: there is no national format, so each institution is its own config.

delivery.description: `hybrid` is real and not a placeholder: WAEC's Nov/Dec GCE has run objective papers on screen with essays answered in physical booklets. A hybrid exam can only be partly simulated, and the UI must say which part.

sections.description: A section is usually a subject (JAMB) or a paper (WASSCE Paper 1/2/3).

duration_minutes.description: Per-section limit where the exam enforces one. Null means the section shares the exam-level clock, which is how JAMB works: one 2-hour timer across all four subjects, with free movement between them.

answer_choose.description: For theory papers that say 'answer any 4 of 6'. Null means answer everything.

shared_passages.description: Comprehension sections where several questions hang off one passage. The passage is stored once and referenced.

option_labels.description: NOT assumed to be A-D. Research indicates NECO objective papers use five options (A-E) while JAMB and WAEC use four, so any shared options component reads this rather than hard-coding four. Getting this wrong means a student practises eliminating three distractors when the real paper has four.

total_duration_minutes.description: The whole sitting. For JAMB this is 120 and it is the only clock.

free_movement.description: May a candidate return to an earlier question?

cross_section_movement.description: May they move between subjects/papers mid-exam? True for JAMB's subject tabs.

question_grid.description: A numbered grid to jump to any question. Answered/unanswered/flagged state must be shown with a symbol AND a word, never colour alone (v2 §4.2).

show_attempted_count_on_submit.description: JAMB's End Examination dialog states 'Total Questions Attempted is N' before committing. It is the last thing a candidate sees and it should be reproduced.

keyboard.description: Key bindings, as data, so a conformance test can assert them. JAMB's are confirmed verbatim from its own Step-by-Step CBT Manual (see docs/research/EXAM_FORMATS.md): A/B/C/D select, N or RightArrow next, P or LeftArrow previous, Up/Down move, S submit, then Y to end and R to continue on the confirmation dialog.

select_option.description: Map of option label to key, e.g. {"A": "a", "B": "b"}.

scale_max.description: The exam's own scale. 400 for UTME -- a result must be reported the way the real exam reports it, or a student cannot calibrate against a target like 'JAMB 280+'.

grade_bands.description: WASSCE reports A1-F9 rather than a number.

subject_rules.description: Combination rules, enforced in onboarding with a plain explanation when one is broken rather than a silent rejection.

requires_trade_subject.description: WAEC reportedly introduced this for 2026. Verify before enforcing it against a student.

restricted.description: Subjects only open to certain tracks. WAEC reportedly restricted Economics to Commercial candidates for 2026 -- a rule that would block a Science student from a subject they may already be studying, so it must be verified at source before it is enforced.

source_url.description: The official page or PDF this was taken from. Required. A format nobody can trace cannot be re-checked next season.

verified_on.description: ISO date as a STRING. YAML parses a bare 2026-09-23 into a date object, which is not a JSON string and fails validation, so the loader coerces date and datetime to ISO strings before validating and configs quote them anyway.

confidence.description: `unconfirmed` fields must not drive a student-facing simulation. A config may ship at `probable` with the gaps named in `notes`.

notes.description: What is uncertain, and what to re-check.

then.description: A CBT simulation without key bindings is not a simulation of a CBT exam.
